Summary  
Data source overview: The IJCAI-18 paper “The Facets of Artificial Intelligence: A Framework to Track the Evolution of AI” argues that unclear, volatile boundaries of the AI discipline impede policy, governance and research prioritisation. It proposes a nine-facet analytical framework, demonstrates its use with 50 years of bibliometric data, and releases open datasets and code. The authors claim the framework can guide funding, venue-scope and regulatory decisions, and highlight the need for ability-oriented evaluation.  
EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83] – structure follows all mandatory criteria; paper is mainly conceptual so several interventions are moderately inferred but tightly grounded in stated recommendations.  
Instruction-set improvement: provide explicit examples for meta-level governance papers (no model training) clarifying that lifecycle 6 “Other” is appropriate; clarify handling of “implemented_by” vs “motivates” when an intervention instantiates a concept method.  
Inference strategy justification: Where the authors imply rather than prescribe concrete actions (e.g., compensatory funding) I marked edges with confidence 2 and flagged inference in the rationale.  
Extraction completeness: All reasoning paths from stated problems (risks) through evidence, methods and findings to actionable interventions are captured; 18 nodes, 26 edges, fully connected.  
Key limitations: The source offers no empirical validation of the proposed framework; effectiveness of interventions therefore remains speculative (edge confidence ≤3). The fabric concerns governance rather than technical AI-safety mitigations, so lifecycle classification defaults to 6 Other.
